name: str_starts
title: Detect a match at the start of a string

origin.description: Return TRUE where string starts with pattern. This is str_detect restricted to the beginning of each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern the string must start with. A plain character vector is a regular expression, wrapped as ^(pattern) so alternation stays inside the anchor. fixed and coll compare the start literally or by collation. The empty string and boundary patterns are not allowed.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, invert the logical result. Must be a single TRUE or FALSE.

origin.details: A regular expression is pasted into ^(pattern) and passed to stri_detect_regex with the pattern's regex options. fixed and coll call stri_startswith_fixed and stri_startswith_coll. Recycling, missing values, and names follow str_detect. paste0 turns a missing piece of a modifier pattern into the letters NA before the anchor is added.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_starts(fruit, "p")
writeLines(paste0('str_starts(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "p") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Return true where string starts with pattern.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is wrapped as ^(pattern) and searched as a regular expression. fixed and coll use the stringi start matchers. The empty string and boundary are errors.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, invert each real match. Must be True or False.

translation.details: The grouped anchor keeps a|b inside the start test, so a string that starts with b matches. Options come from pattern_opts. A missing pattern element is pasted as the letters NA, giving ^(NA). Names and recycling follow str_detect.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.detect import str_starts
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_starts(fruit, "p")
words = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print('str_starts(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "p") returns ' + words + '.')
